common_name: Dragon Slayer Adam's Needle (Compact Powder-Blue Evergreen Yucca)

planting.note: Plant container-grown offsets or divisions in spring in well-drained, average to poor soil in full sun; Dragon Slayer tolerates heat, drought, and a wide pH range once established.

directions: Dragon Slayer is a 2026 Proven Winners selection of hybrid Yucca that forms a tight, symmetrical rosette of stiff, powder-blue evergreen foliage edged with fine white filaments. In summer it sends up a flower stalk bearing clusters of creamy white bells well above the foliage mound. The plant tolerates poor, dry soil and extreme heat, needs almost no supplemental water once established, and resists deer and rabbit browsing, making it a low-care focal point for borders and containers.

common_name: Bloomerang Showmound Reblooming Lilac (Dwarf Mounding Fragrant White Lilac)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil in full sun; prune immediately after the spring flush to encourage the late-summer rebloom.

directions: Bloomerang Showmound is a dwarf, mound-forming lilac bred for small-space gardens, reaching only about knee height while covering itself in fragrant, creamy-white flower clusters. Unlike most lilacs it blooms twice, flowering in spring like other lilacs and then again in late summer on new wood. Its compact, rounded habit and repeat bloom make it useful as a low hedge, container thriller, or foundation planting where a full-sized lilac would be too large.

common_name: Kodiak Spiced Bush Honeysuckle (Orange-Flushed Foliage Diervilla)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average to clay soil in full to part sun; little pruning is needed beyond occasional spring shaping or a rejuvenation cut every few years.

directions: Kodiak Spiced is a native-heritage Diervilla selection whose foliage opens warm orange-bronze in spring and deepens through a mix of green and orange tones into fall, paired with clusters of bright yellow, nectar-rich flowers that open through summer. It forms a tidy, rounded 3-4 foot shrub that tolerates clay soil and part shade, and draws bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds to its blooms. Its colorful foliage and easy care make it a candidate for hedging, mass planting, or mixed borders where many bush honeysuckles would look plain.

common_name: Safari Lava Flow African Phlox (Scarlet-Red Heat-Tolerant Jamesbrittenia)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost in well-drained soil in full to part sun; feed weekly and keep soil evenly moist but not soggy for the longest bloom season.

directions: Safari Lava Flow is a Jamesbrittenia, a bacopa relative bred for far better heat and humidity tolerance, smothering itself in hot scarlet-red flowers with golden centers from spring until frost. Its low, trailing-mounded habit spreads wider than it is tall, making it well suited to hanging baskets, window boxes, and the edges of sunny containers. The variety flowers continuously without deadheading and keeps performing through summer conditions that cause many bacopa types to stall out.

common_name: Sweet Caroline Sweetheart Shadowstorm Sweet Potato Vine (Near-Black Variegated Heart-Leaf Vine)

planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or container plants after the last frost in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full to part sun; grown for its dark variegated foliage rather than bloom.

directions: Shadowstorm is an addition to the Sweet Caroline Sweetheart line of ornamental sweet potato vines, with heart-shaped leaves that open fresh green and gradually darken to a near-black background mottled with flecks of green, giving a shadowy, camouflage-like look distinct from older solid-colored selections. It grows into a fuller, bushier mound than older variegated sweet potato vines, which tend to need frequent pinching to stay tidy. Grown strictly for foliage rather than bloom, it trails well from hanging baskets and mixed containers and holds its color and habit through summer heat with minimal upkeep.

common_name: Campfire Red Ember Apache Beggarticks (Fiery Red Bidens with Yellow Eye)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; feed weekly with water-soluble fertilizer for continuous bloom through frost.

directions: Campfire Red Ember is a Bidens ferulifolia selection covered in small, fiery red flowers with a contrasting orange-yellow center from planting until hard frost, a sibling to the series' bicolor 'Fireburst' but a solid-color departure from it. It forms a dense, low mound and sets very little seed, which appears to let the plant redirect its energy into nonstop flower production instead. Full sun and regular feeding keep it blooming heavily all season in beds, containers, and mass plantings, and its flowers reliably draw in pollinators.
